newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Celtech to list on S.Africa JSE Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Celtech to list on S.Africa JSE Wednesday.

text.p: Celtron Technologies Ltd, which is to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Wednesday, said it forecast earnings for the year to end September at 13.46 cents a share rising to 70.83 cents in 1998.

Celtech, which will debut on the JSE's venture capital market with 59.78 million ordinary shares, operates in the cellular communications industry. Business includes mobile phone rental and the sale of vehicle tracking systems using cellular technology.
It said it expected to declare a dividend of 4.04 cents this year which was seen jumping to 21.25 cents next year.
Celtech cautioned in a published announcement that listings on the venture capital market were inherently risky but directors added that they were confident of achieving projected earnings.
Sponsoring brokers Lowenthal & Co said on Wednesday that shares, which had been issued at 78 cents each, had been placed privately with some being taken up by institutions.
"Institutions were offered stock and quite a few took it up," a spokesman told Reuters.
He said black expowerment firm New Africa Investments Ltd had taken a 10 percent stake in Celtech at a purchase price of 1.75 rand a share.
He said Celtech's reason for listing was to raise capital to finance a number of big contracts.
